title: Beat Map
description: The measured rhythm of a film's audio track. Produced by audio_beatmap at the score stage and consumed by scene_plan, which lands scene boundaries on its beats. Every number here is measured from the delivered audio - never copied from what a generator was asked for. ACE-Step has been asked for 90 BPM on this machine and delivered 117.5 (DECISIONS, PLAN WP6), so a plan timed from the request rather than the measurement is wrong by 30%.

source.description: Project-relative path of the audio this was measured from, e.g. assets/music/project_audio.mp3

tempo_bpm.description: Measured tempo. Absent when the track has no stable pulse - which is honest, not a failure. A caller with no tempo should pace by phrase and never hard-cut to a grid.

requested_tempo_bpm.description: What the generator was asked for, when the track was generated. Recorded only so the gap with tempo_bpm stays visible; nothing may time from this field.

beats.description: Beat positions in seconds from the start of the track, ascending.

downbeats.description: Bar starts in seconds, a subset of beats. A cut on a downbeat reads stronger than a cut on any other beat.

sections.description: Musical structure - intro, verse, chorus. Scene groupings should respect these before they respect individual beats.

energy.description: Relative loudness/density of this section, 0-1 within this track only. Not comparable across tracks.

measured_by.description: Which analyzer produced this, e.g. 'vrgdg:analyze_audio' or 'librosa'. One analyzer per map - never merge two, and never re-measure by ear.

confidence.description: How much the grid can be trusted. 'strong': a genuine pulse, safe to hard-cut to. 'weak': a metronome the tracker imposed on calm music - pace by phrase instead. 'none': no usable rhythm. Guessing this as 'strong' is how a calm track gets cut like a dance track.
